title: Flip a one-third-full water bottle end over end so it lands standing upright on the desk pad
instruction: Flip the water bottle so that it lands standing upright on the desk pad.
context: The water bottle flip was a worldwide craze from 2016, tried by most teenagers and many adults. Done with one hand: the bottle has to leave the fingers turning about once end over end, so its water slides along it, slows the spin and lets it land base first. Flick too little and it lands on its cap or side; too hard or let go late and it over-rotates and topples.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), on the table top. (1) Grey felt desk pad, 40 x 40 x 0.3 cm, taped flat, centred at x 36, y -16. (2) Capped 500 ml (16.9 fl oz) PET water bottle (Poland Spring size), 6.2 cm across, 20.3 cm tall, cap 3.1 cm across, 15 g empty with cap, filled with 170 ml of water to a line drawn 6.2 cm above its base (185 g in all), standing upright on the pad with its base centred at x 30, y -6. Distractors, ignored by the scorer: (3) paper notebook, 22.9 x 17.0 x 1.0 cm, 120 g, centred at x 20, y 27; (4) ceramic mug, 11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 300 g, at x 42, y 22; (5) apple, about 7 cm across, 180 g, at x 56, y 12. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: A flight starts when the bottle leaves a gripper (no finger within 12 mm of it, its lowest point more than 12 mm above the pad or table) and ends at its first touch of a finger, the table, the pad or anything else. It is a flip if the bottle's axis turns 240 deg or more end over end between the last moment in the hand and that touch, and no finger touches it in the air. Score: no flip: 0; a flip that comes down on the table or pad (lowest point within 3 cm of it at the touch): 0.25; such a flip whose first touchdown is base first on the pad (axis within 45 deg of upright, base centre over the pad): 0.5; after a flip, with no finger touching the bottle since, it stands on its base on the pad (axis within 10 deg of vertical, base flat on the pad within 5 mm, base centre on the pad), still (under 2 cm/s and 0.3 rad/s), every finger 5 cm or more away, for 2 s: 1.0. The best level reached counts; any number of attempts within the run limit. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Doing nothing, or setting the bottle down upright, scores 0. Real trial: a 240 fps side video gives the turn and the touchdown; a photo and protractor check the final stand.
reset_notes: Top the bottle up to its 170 ml line if any water was lost (it is capped, so normally none), dry it, and stand it on its taped circle on the pad.
fidelity: Bottle and cap are one rigid custom lathe shape (body, shoulder and neck colliders, flat base; the real base has five feet). The 170 g of water is two 85 g masses sliding along the bottle's axis with damping, after the tennis-ball model of Dekker et al. (2018), its travel set to their spin-down ratio (0.30); no sloshing sideways. Felt pad is a rigid box. No bounce (restitution 0). Friction estimates: bottle 0.6/0.5, pad 0.8/0.7. Distractors are SimReady props.
